method:
Build docs/countries.json for the country ranking page (docs/countries.html).

Per country:
  - price per acre: median USD/acre of land listings in the app (falls back to
    every listing with an acreage when a country has fewer than 5 land rows)
  - quality of life: UN Human Development Index 2023 (HDR 2025 data file)
  - climate: monthly normals 2016-2025 from the Open-Meteo archive (ERA5),
    averaged over three sample points taken from where that country's listings
    actually are (20th / 50th / 80th percentile of latitude)
  - tax: estimated cost for a foreign individual buying a ~US$1M second home and
    holding it 10 years: one-off purchase taxes + foreign-buyer surcharges + 10x
    annual property/wealth tax, as % of price. Rough, hand-maintained, see TAX.

Usage: python3 scripts/country_stats.py   (climate cached in scripts/geo/climate_cache.json)

tax.note: acquisition + registration tax on assessed value; fixed-asset + city-planning tax ~1.7% of assessed value/yr

income_tax.note: 45% national + 10% local. Non-permanent residents (first 5 of 10 yrs) only pay on foreign income they bring into Japan.

residency.note: resident only if your domicile is in Japan or you've lived there a year; 90-day visa-free visits stay non-resident.

bands.extras: National tax only. Add a 2.1% reconstruction surtax on the national tax (through 2037), so the top national rate is 45.945%. Add a flat 10% local inhabitant tax on the prior year's income, plus a per-capita levy of about JPY 5,000. Top combined rate is about 55.945%.
bands.capital_gains: Listed shares: 20.315% separate taxation (15.315% national + 5% local). Real estate: 20.315% if held more than 5 years, 39.63% if 5 years or less.
bands.dividends: Listed company dividends: 20.315% final (separate taxation option). Alternatively aggregated with a dividend credit.

tax.note: provincial land transfer tax; federal ban on foreign purchase of homes in cities until 2027 (rural/recreational exempt); BC adds 20% for foreigners in some regions

income_tax.note: federal + provincial (BC/ON ~53.5%); worldwide income.

home.note: a year-round home is a significant tie: CRA can treat you as resident under 183 days if your ties elsewhere are weak.

bands.capital_gains: 50% of the gain is included in income at marginal rates (the planned 2/3 inclusion increase was cancelled). Principal residence is exempt.
bands.dividends: Eligible dividends are grossed up 38% with a federal and provincial dividend tax credit. The top combined BC rate on eligible dividends is about 36.5%.

tax.note: state/county transfer tax ~0.5-1%; property tax ~1.1%/yr (MA)

income_tax.note: 37% federal + state (MA 9% over $1M, UT 4.65%); worldwide income. US citizens pay this wherever they live.

residency.note: 183-day test weighted over 3 years: coming every year, 122+ days/yr makes you resident (121 is safe). Closer-connection exception (Form 8840) can protect you up to 182 days. ESTA visitors max 90 days per visit; longer needs a B-2 visa.

bands.extras: Federal only, single filer, applied to taxable income after the $16,100 standard deduction. State and local income taxes are extra (0% to about 13%). 3.8% NIIT on investment income above $200k MAGI. 0.9% Additional Medicare tax on wages above $200k.
bands.capital_gains: Long-term: 0/15/20% (single: 0% up to about $49k of taxable income, 20% above about $545k), plus 3.8% NIIT. Short-term: ordinary rates. Home sale exclusion of $250k.
bands.dividends: Qualified dividends: 0/15/20% (+3.8% NIIT). Non-qualified: ordinary rates.

tax.note: 3.5% Grunderwerbsteuer + 1.1% land-register fee; Grundsteuer tiny; EU nationals treated as locals

income_tax.note: 50% above ~€100k, 55% above €1M; capital income 27.5% flat; worldwide.

home.note: any home you can use makes you resident. Second-home rule: if your centre of life has been abroad 5+ yrs, using the Austrian home on no more than 70 days a year keeps you non-resident (keep a day log).

bands.extras: The 55% band is temporary (in place to 2029). There is no local income tax.
bands.capital_gains: 27.5% flat on securities and crypto. 30% on real estate (ImmoESt). Main residence is often exempt.
bands.dividends: 27.5% flat (KESt)

tax.note: IMT ~6% + 0.8% stamp duty; IMI 0.3-0.45% + AIMI above €600k

income_tax.note: 48% + 5% solidarity; 28% flat on investment income. IFICI ('NHR 2.0'): 20% on qualifying jobs and most foreign income exempt for 10 yrs, if you qualify.

home.note: a home kept as your habitual residence can make you resident under 183 days.

bands.extras: Solidarity surcharge: 2.5% on taxable income from €80k to €250k, and 5% above €250k. IFICI (the 'NHR 2.0' regime): 20% flat for qualifying new residents.
bands.capital_gains: Securities: 28% flat, or optional aggregation (with reliefs for long holdings from 2025). Real estate: 50% of the gain is added to progressive income.
bands.dividends: 28% flat, or optional aggregation with 50% of the dividend included.

tax.note: foreigners pay 4% flat stamp duty; some states add a foreign levy (e.g. Penang 3%); RM1M+ minimum price for foreigners in most states

income_tax.note: foreign income brought in by individuals is exempt until end-2036.

residency.note: 182 days, or shorter stays linked to longer ones across years.

bands.extras: Territorial basis. Foreign-source income remitted by individuals is exempt until 2036 (conditions apply).
bands.capital_gains: No general CGT for individuals (the 2024 CGT applies to companies). RPGT on real property for citizens and PRs: 30% (held up to 3 years), 20% (year 4), 15% (year 5), 0% (year 6 onwards).
bands.dividends: Single-tier dividends are exempt. However, a 2% dividend tax applies on dividends above RM100k a year from YA2025.

tax.note: transfer fee 2% (often split); foreigners cannot own land: condo or 30-yr lease only

income_tax.note: since 2024, foreign income is taxed if brought into Thailand (not if kept abroad). LTR-visa holders: foreign income exempt.

bands.extras: Since 2024, foreign-source income of residents is taxable when remitted to Thailand.
bands.capital_gains: Gains on SET-listed shares are exempt for individuals. Other gains are taxed as ordinary income. Real estate sale is subject to withholding on assessed value plus 3.3% specific business tax if held less than 5 years.
bands.dividends: 10% final withholding (optional). Alternatively included at progressive rates with a dividend credit.

tax.note: notary + registry; contribuciones ~1% of fiscal value (rural land often exempt)

income_tax.note: foreigners pay only on Chilean income for their first 3 years, then worldwide.

residency.note: 183 days in any 12 months (or across 2 consecutive years).

bands.extras: Impuesto Global Complementario. In UTA: exempt to 13.5, then 30, 50, 70, 90, 120, 310. The same factors apply monthly (in UTM) for the employment tax.
bands.capital_gains: Generally taxed in IGC. Gains on listed shares meeting market-presence rules: 10% sole tax (since 2023). Housing gains: exempt up to 8,000 UF lifetime.
bands.dividends: Included in IGC with a credit for corporate tax (partial integration, generally 65% of the credit is usable).
bands.why: The source is a secondary site, not SII (its arithmetic checks against the UTA). The capital gains and dividend notes are from memory.

tax.note: 2% PCC on resale; property tax per m², very low; farmland restricted for non-farmers

income_tax.note: 32% + 4% solidarity above PLN 1M; 19% on capital income; 19% flat option for business income.

home.note: centre of vital interests in Poland makes you resident.

tax.note: notary + registration; building tax ~0.1-0.2%/yr; non-EU buyers cannot own land directly

income_tax.note: 10% flat income tax (plus health contributions); dividends 16%.

home.note: centre of vital interests in Romania makes you resident.

bands.extras: Flat rate. Employee social contributions are significant: CAS 25% (pension) + CASS 10% (health). CASS of 10% also applies on investment income above minimum-wage-based thresholds.
bands.capital_gains: Securities via Romanian brokers: 3% (held 1 year or more) / 6% (less than 1 year). Otherwise 16%. Real estate: a transfer tax of 3% or 6% of value, depending on the value threshold.
bands.why: The capital gains and dividend changes under Law 141/2025 are from memory; the PwC page I read did not state them.

tax.note: ITBI 2-3% + registry; IPTU/ITR; limits on foreign ownership of rural land

income_tax.note: 27.5% on salary; 15% on offshore investments since 2024; new minimum tax on high earners from 2026.

residency.note: 183 days in 12 months; a permanent visa makes you resident from day one.

tax.note: BPHTB 5% + notary; foreigners only via Hak Pakai (right-of-use) or company

income_tax.note: worldwide; skilled expats can elect Indonesian-income-only for the first 4 years.

bands.extras: Personal relief (PTKP) of IDR 54m for a single filer, deducted before the bands.
bands.capital_gains: Listed share sales: 0.1% final tax on gross proceeds. Land and building transfers: 2.5% final tax on gross value. Other gains: progressive rates.
bands.dividends: 10% final tax. Exempt if reinvested in Indonesia (conditions apply).

tax.note: no stamp duty or capital-gains tax; council rates; foreigners mostly banned from buying existing homes

income_tax.note: new residents: most foreign income exempt for the first 4 years; no capital-gains tax.

home.note: a 'permanent place of abode' in NZ makes you resident whatever the days.

bands.extras: ACC earners' levy of about 1.75% on earnings (capped). Foreign investment fund (FIF) regime: 5% deemed return on offshore portfolios above NZD 50k.
bands.capital_gains: No general CGT. The bright-line test taxes residential property sold within 2 years at marginal rates.
bands.dividends: Taxed at marginal rates with imputation credits (28% company credit).

bands.extras: Medicare levy of 2%. Medicare levy surcharge of 1% to 1.5% for higher earners without private hospital cover. The 2025-26 lowest rate was 16%.
bands.capital_gains: Taxed at marginal rates with a 50% discount for assets held more than 12 months. Main residence is exempt.
bands.dividends: Taxed at marginal rates with franking credits (refundable).

United Kingdom.price_basis: estates incl. houses (few listings: not comparable)

tax.note: Scotland: LBTT up to 12% (~10% effective at £2M) + 8% ADS if you own another home anywhere (reclaimable if it becomes your main home); council tax

income_tax.note: Scotland 48% top rate; new arrivals: foreign income and gains exempt for the first 4 years (FIG regime).

home.note: Statutory Residence Test: a home available to you plus 90+ days the year before = 2 ties, so returning visitors become resident from 121 days.

bands.extras: Scottish non-savings, non-dividend income. The £12,570 personal allowance is withdrawn at £1 per £2 above £100k, so the effective marginal rate is about 67.5% between £100k and £125,140. Employee NIC is 8% / 2% (UK-wide).
bands.capital_gains: UK-wide: 18% (basic) / 24% (higher), annual exempt amount £3,000. Main residence is exempt.
bands.dividends: UK-wide rates (not Scottish): from April 2026, 10.75% / 35.75% / 39.35%, with a £500 allowance.
bands.why: The Scottish bands are from gov.uk. The 2026/27 dividend rate rise (+2pp, announced in the Nov 2025 Budget) is from memory and was not verified.

France.price_basis: estates incl. houses (few listings: not comparable)

tax.note: notary + registration ~7.5-8% on resale; taxe foncière; IFI wealth tax above €1.3M

income_tax.note: 45% + 4% high-income surcharge; ~30% flat on investment income; impatriate regime for workers moving in.

home.note: your 'foyer' (main home/family) or main work in France makes you resident; a holiday home alone doesn't.

bands.extras: Thresholds are per household part (quotient familial). High-income surtax (CEHR): 3% above €250k single, 4% above €500k. CDHR: a minimum effective rate of 20% above €250k. Social charges of 9.7% on earned income (CSG/CRDS), partly deductible.
bands.capital_gains: PFU flat tax of 31.4% (12.8% income tax + 18.6% social charges). Real estate: 19% + 17.2% social charges, with holding-period taper (exempt after 22 / 30 years). Main home is exempt.
bands.dividends: PFU of 31.4% from 2026, or optional progressive scale with a 40% allowance plus social charges.

tax.note: transfer duty up to 13% above ~R12M; municipal rates; register foreign funds with the Reserve Bank to repatriate later

income_tax.note: worldwide; dividends 20%, capital gains effectively up to ~18%.

home.note: 'ordinarily resident' if SA is your real home.

residency.note: physical-presence test: 91+ days every year for 6 years and 915+ in the last 5 (so ~183/yr if you come every year).

tax.note: 9% registration tax on a second-home resale (on cadastral value); IMU on second homes

income_tax.note: 26% on investment income. New residents can pay a flat €200k/yr on ALL foreign income for 15 yrs; 7% flat for foreign pensioners in small southern towns.

home.note: your habitual abode or centre of interests in Italy makes you resident.

bands.extras: National IRPEF only. Add a regional surcharge of about 1.23% to 3.33% and a municipal surcharge of 0% to 0.9%, so the top marginal rate is about 47%. The middle rate was cut from 35% to 33% by the 2026 Budget.
bands.capital_gains: 26% substitute tax on financial assets (12.5% on government bonds). Real estate: gains on property held more than 5 years are exempt; otherwise IRPEF, or a 26% substitute tax.
bands.dividends: 26% final withholding

income_tax.note: savings income 19-30%. Beckham law: 24% on Spanish work income, foreign income exempt, for 6 yrs. Regional wealth tax.

home.note: centre of economic interests or family in Spain makes you resident.

bands.extras: These bands are state + standard regional combined (each half). Actual regional scales vary: the top combined rate is about 45% in Madrid and 50% to 54% in Valencia and Catalonia.
bands.capital_gains: Savings scale: 19% (to €6k), 21% (to €50k), 23% (to €200k), 27% (to €300k), 30% above. Same for real estate.
bands.dividends: Same savings scale (19% to 30%)
bands.why: The bands are the standard combined scale. The real combined rate depends on the autonomous community.

income_tax.note: non-dom option: flat €100k/yr on all foreign income (needs €500k investment); 7% flat for foreign pensioners; half-tax for relocating workers.

home.note: permanent home/centre of vital interests in Greece makes you resident.

bands.extras: General scale under Law 5246/2025. Lower scales apply for taxpayers with children or under 30. Rental income has its own scale (15/25/35/45%). The solidarity contribution is abolished. Non-dom regime: €100k lump sum.
bands.capital_gains: 15% on securities (listed holdings under 0.5% are exempt). Real estate CGT of 15% is suspended through 2026.
bands.dividends: 5% final withholding

tax.note: 3% transfer tax; holiday-home property tax since 2025

income_tax.note: top rate 30-33% depending on city; 12% on capital income.

home.note: owning or renting a home you use (domicile) can make you resident.

income_tax.note: 9-15% progressive.

income_tax.note: non-dom residents: 0% on dividends and interest for 17 years; foreign pensions 5%.

home.note: 60-day rule: with a Cyprus home, a local job/company and no other tax residence you can choose to be resident after 60 days (then non-dom: 0% on dividends).

bands.extras: GHS (health) contribution of 2.65% on income, including dividends, capped at €180k. Non-doms are exempt from SDC for 17 years.
bands.capital_gains: 20% CGT only on Cyprus immovable property (and shares in companies holding it). Securities gains are exempt.
bands.dividends: Special Defence Contribution of 5% (17% before 2026) for domiciled residents, in place of income tax. 0% for non-doms.

income_tax.note: non-domiciled residents pay nothing on foreign income they keep abroad (minimum €5k tax).

home.note: intention to live in Malta makes you resident.

bands.extras: Single-rate scale. Residents who are not domiciled are taxed on a remittance basis, with a €5k minimum tax. Social security of about 10% (capped).
bands.capital_gains: Malta property: final tax of 8% on transfer value (10% if acquired before 2004; 5% for disposals within 5 years in some cases). Securities: gains are taxed at progressive rates, but listed securities are generally exempt.
bands.dividends: Full imputation: tax credit for 35% corporate tax, so usually no extra tax at top rate. 15% final option on certain investment income.
bands.why: The capital gains and dividend notes are from memory.

income_tax.note: no personal income tax.

home.note: 90 days + a permanent home + UAE residence visa or job gets you a UAE tax-residence certificate.

bands.extras: No personal income tax. 9% corporate tax applies to individuals' business turnover above AED 1m (personal investment and real estate income are excluded).
bands.capital_gains: None for individuals (personal investments)
bands.dividends: None

bands.extras: Territorial system: foreign-source income is not taxed.
bands.capital_gains: Real estate: 10% on gain (3% of sale price paid in advance). Shares: 10% on gain (5% of price withheld).
bands.dividends: 10% withholding on nominative shares from Panama-source profits. 5% on foreign-source or certain zone profits.

bands.extras: This is the annual scale for self-employed and business income. Employees use a separate monthly salary scale (0/10/15/20/25%). Territorial system: foreign income is generally not taxed.
bands.capital_gains: 15% on capital gains (Law 9635). For assets held before 2019, an option of 2.25% of gross price.
bands.dividends: 15% final withholding
bands.why: The employment monthly scale was not verified. The capital gains figures are from memory.

home.note: setting up your home (casa habitación) in Mexico makes you resident; with homes in two countries your centre of vital interests decides.

residency.note: no fixed day count; 183 is a rule of thumb.

bands.extras: Annual table, applied as fixed fee + marginal rate. States levy payroll taxes on employers, not on individuals.
bands.capital_gains: Shares on the Mexican stock exchange: 10% on gain. Real estate and other gains: progressive rates (with averaging). Main home exempt up to a UDI cap.
bands.dividends: Additional 10% withholding on dividends from post-2014 profits. Dividends are also aggregated with a corporate tax credit.

bands.extras: IRPF on labour income. Thresholds are set in BPC (7/10/15/30/50/75/115 times 12 BPC) and indexed each year, so 2026 thresholds are a few percent higher. New residents can elect a 10- or 11-year holiday on foreign capital income.
bands.capital_gains: 12% (often on a deemed basis, e.g. 20% of price, giving an effective 2.4%). Real estate is the same.
bands.dividends: 7% on Uruguayan dividends. 12% on foreign dividends (if no holiday applies).
bands.why: The bands are 2025 values; 2026 BPC indexation was not verified. The 7% dividend rate is from memory; PwC only states 12% for capital income.

bands.extras: The 14% to 42% zone is a linear-progressive formula, not a flat band. Solidarity surcharge: 5.5% of income tax, only above about €20k of tax (taxable income of about €73k+ single), with full rate from about €105k. Church tax: 8% to 9% of income tax if a member.
bands.capital_gains: Securities: Abgeltungsteuer 25% + soli = 26.375% (+ church tax), with a €1,000 saver allowance. Real estate: exempt after 10 years (or if owner-occupied); otherwise marginal rates.
bands.why: The PwC page shows 2025 figures (€12,096 / €68,430). The 2026 figures (€12,348 / €69,879) come from German tax press found by search. The 14-42% zone is a smooth formula; the calculator treats it as steps, so it under-states tax for incomes between ~€12k and ~€70k.
